children: The CAC 40 fell 0.2% to 8,263 on Thursday, extending losses for a fourth consecutive session and slipping to its lowest level since mid-June, led by weakness in the luxury sector.
LVMH dropped 1.9%, while Hermès and Kering both shed 2.4%, as the sector remained under pressure despite early signs of stabilizing consumer sentiment.

Investors remained cautious as stimulus measures in China, the industry's most important growth market, have yet to translate into a meaningful recovery in demand, leaving luxury groups struggling to regain momentum after the disruption caused by the Iran conflict.

In contrast, Legrand rose 2.6% after Deutsche Bank upgraded the stock to "Buy" from "Hold." Further weighing on sentiment, final data showed the Composite PMI falling to 48.5 in August from 49.4 in July, as a sharper contraction in services (48 vs 49.6) more than offset an expansion in manufacturing (51.1 vs 49.8).

title: French Stocks Hit Near 3-Month Low
